llm.reply:
The knowledge graph links Lynch syndrome to a set of mismatch-repair and other genes, including NCBIGene:4292, mutL homolog 1 [10]. The condition is indexed as Lynch syndrome [7]. Several related clinical studies are registered, and no specific clinical variant records were returned.

## Mismatch Repair Genes

NCBIGene:4436 is mutS homolog 2 [11]. NCBIGene:2956 is mutS homolog 6 [8]. NCBIGene:5395 is PMS1 homolog 2, mismatch repair system component [14]. NCBIGene:27030 is mutL homolog 3 [6]. NCBIGene:5378 is PMS1 homolog 1, mismatch repair system component [13].

## Other Associated Genes

NCBIGene:4072 is epithelial cell adhesion molecule [9]. NCBIGene:7048 is transforming growth factor beta receptor 2 [16]. NCBIGene:999 is cadherin 1 [17]. NCBIGene:4763 is neurofibromin 1 [12]. NCBIGene:6224 is ribosomal protein S20 [15].

## Clinical Studies

One trial is Implementation of a New Strategy to Identify HNPCC Patients [1]. Another is Hereditary Nonpolyposis Colorectal Cancer in Taiwan-Related Genetic Study and Clinical Applications [2]. A third is Psychosocial Aspects of Genetic Testing for Hereditary Nonpolyposis Colon Cancer [3]. A fourth is Registry for Women Who Are At Risk Or May Have Lynch Syndrome [5].

## Records and Literature

The MedGen record is titled Lynch syndrome [19]. The literature index also uses the entity Colorectal Neoplasms Hereditary Nonpolyposis [23]. One review is Differentiating Lynch-like from Lynch syndrome. [22]. Another review is Lynch Syndrome Genetics and Clinical Implications. [30].

The knowledge graph links the Lynch syndrome disease record to a set of genes that is dominated by DNA mismatch repair components [7]. It also returns several clinical studies on hereditary nonpolyposis colorectal cancer (HNPCC) and Lynch syndrome. None of the retrieved records covers individual clinical variants.

## Mismatch Repair Genes

The associated genes include NCBIGene:4292, mutL homolog 1 [10]. They also include NCBIGene:4436, mutS homolog 2 [11]. NCBIGene:2956, mutS homolog 6, is linked as well [8]. So is NCBIGene:5395, PMS1 homolog 2, mismatch repair system component [14]. Further mismatch repair genes are NCBIGene:27030, mutL homolog 3 [6], and NCBIGene:5378, PMS1 homolog 1, mismatch repair system component [13].

## Other Associated Genes

Several genes outside mismatch repair are also linked. These include NCBIGene:4072, epithelial cell adhesion molecule [9]. Another is NCBIGene:7048, transforming growth factor beta receptor 2 [16]. NCBIGene:999, cadherin 1, appears too [17]. So do NCBIGene:4763, neurofibromin 1 [12], and NCBIGene:6224, ribosomal protein S20 [15].

## Clinical Studies

One study evaluates a new strategy for identifying HNPCC patients [1]. A second is a Taiwanese genetic study of HNPCC [2]. A third examines psychosocial aspects of HNPCC genetic testing [3]. A fourth compares an educational CD-ROM with standard informed consent for colorectal cancer patients or families [4]. There is also a registry for women who are at risk of, or may have, Lynch syndrome [5].

## Condition Record and Literature

The condition has a MedGen record titled Lynch syndrome [19]. Literature entities include Lynch syndrome I (site-specific colonic cancer) [20]. They also include Lynch Syndrome II [26] and Colorectal Neoplasms Hereditary Nonpolyposis [23]. Related publications include PMID 21508689 [21] and PMID 24468183 [24]. Further publications are PMID 34210484 [27] and PMID 34798986 [29]. One paper is titled Lynch syndrome. [18] Another is Differentiating Lynch-like from Lynch syndrome. [22] A third is Overview of Prostate Cancer Genetic Testing. [25] A fourth is Identification of Lynch Syndrome. [28] A fifth is Lynch Syndrome Genetics and Clinical Implications. [30]
